author: Swinhoe, 1863
summary: 국내에서는 해마다 10건 미만 기록되는 길잃은새로, 주로 5월과 9~10월에 서해의 섬에서 울음소리로 확인된다. 일본 혼슈·시코쿠·규슈의 높은 산 아고산대 숲에서 번식하고, 타이완·필리핀 등 동남아시아에서 겨울을 난다. 쇠솔새·큰솔새와 생김새가 매우 비슷하나 아랫면이 더 노랗고, 울음소리가 더 낮고 탁하다.

points.en: pale lower mandible with a dark tip
bright olive-green upperparts, greener than Arctic and Kamchatka Leaf Warblers
underparts washed yellow, yellower than its relatives

similar.how: 쇠솔새는 아랫면이 더 희고 노란 기가 적으며, 울음소리가 솔새보다 높다.

art.subject: Japanese Leaf Warbler (Phylloscopus xanthodryas), adult, as seen on Korean islands during spring migration: crown and upperparts fairly bright olive-green with a yellowish tone; long yellowish-white supercilium that stops short of the forehead; dark olive eye-stripe running to the bill base; ear-coverts mottled olive and yellow; wings darker with green edges and a narrow yellowish-white bar on the greater coverts, sometimes a second faint bar on the median coverts; underparts whitish washed pale yellow, the yellow strongest on the throat, flanks and undertail coverts. Bill dark with a pale orange-yellow lower mandible; dark eye; legs pale pinkish-brown.
art.pose: foraging among fresh leaves in the canopy, side view
art.scene: deciduous trees on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in late May; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in spring, side view foraging among fresh leaves in the canopy: bright olive-green upperparts, long pale supercilium above a broad dark eye-stripe, single pale wing-bar, long wings, underparts washed yellow, pale lower mandible with a dark tip

adult, side view perched on a twig: bright olive-green crown and back, long pale supercilium, broad dark eye-stripe, single pale wing-bar on the long folded wings, yellow-washed underparts, pale lower mandible tipped dark
art.build: Medium-sized leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow but larger and longer-winged than Yellow-browed Warbler, with a rather flat crown and a fairly stout, pointed bill shorter than the head. Legs medium length, pale. Long wings with a long primary projection; the wingtips reach well down the tail. Tail medium length, square-ended. Forages actively in the canopy, picking insects from leaves.
avoid: Do not paint it dull grey-green with whitish underparts like Arctic Warbler (Phylloscopus borealis); this species is yellower above and below.
Do not paint a pale crown stripe (Eastern Crowned Warbler).
Do not paint two bold white wing-bars (Two-barred Warbler); the bar is narrow and the second is faint or absent.
